preconditions.description: The number of cities n is a positive integer between 2 and 200,000 inclusive.
The number of roads is exactly n - 1, forming a tree structure.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and u != v for u, v in roads)
preconditions.description: Each road connects two distinct cities within the valid range [1, n].

postconditions.expression: k == min_days and all(1 <= d_i <= len(roads) for d_i in day_counts) and sum(day_counts) == len(roads)
postconditions.description: k is the minimum number of days required to repair all roads, and each day's road count is valid.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= road_num <= len(roads) for day in day_schedule for road_num in day)
postconditions.description: Each road number in the schedule is valid and corresponds to the input order.

postconditions.expression: all(len(set(road) & set(roads)) == 2 for road in day_schedule)
postconditions.description: Each road in a day's schedule connects two distinct cities, ensuring brigades can repair it.

postconditions.expression: all(len(set(city for road in day for city in road)) == len(day) * 2 for day in day_schedule)
postconditions.description: No two roads in the same day share a city, ensuring brigades are not overbooked.

candidate_issues.instruction: Add a postcondition ensuring that the schedule is feasible: every road is repaired exactly once, and the repair assignments respect the constraint that no city's brigade is assigned to more than one road per day.
candidate_issues.task_evidence: To repair some road, you need two teams based in the cities connected by the road to work simultaneously for one day. Both brigades repair one road for the whole day and cannot take part in repairing other roads on that day.
